method: ChargerLAB teardown names this exact model (page title "Teardown of EHOM EP1650 Portable Power Station (EP1650-3)", label "Model is EP1650-3") and shows a 1024 Wh LFP pack, a bidirectional inverter module, a battery protection PCB and a fast-charging PCB.

comps.spec: LFP pack, 1024 Wh per page: 16 EVE IFR40135 cells (20 Ah, 3.2 V, 64 Wh each). Page says eight cells form a set and two sets are in series.

Bidirectional inverter module, pure sine wave output. AC outlet rated 1650 W with a peak of 2700 W; the label reads 230 V 50 Hz 7.2 A 1650 W and the text says 220 V AC. AC input label: 220-240 V 50 Hz 10 A 1200 W.
DC input 11-55 V, 8 A max, 400 W max. Page says the fast-charging PCB is equipped with an MPPT circuit.
SinoWealth SH367309 battery protection chip: overcharge, over-discharge, temperature, overcurrent and short-circuit protection.
PCsemic PCSL016N08NL in TOLL-1L package, 80 V, 1.6 mOhm. Battery protection MOSFETs.
Two 0.3 mOhm current-sense resistors in parallel for battery pack current.
Betterfuse SMD fuse marked 491, 100 A. Protects the battery pack from overcurrent.
NTC thermistor on the protection board, sensing the temperature of the battery protection MOSFETs.
The battery packs are connected through copper sheets.
GigaDevice GD32F303RCT6 MCU on the fast-charging PCB (page lists 120 MHz, 256 KB flash). The page also lists an Espressif ESP32-C3-MINI-1 wireless communication module on the front of the same PCB.
Buzzer, used for reminder.

Four captioned switches: reset and output-switching control on the battery protection PCB, a DC output control button next to the car port buck inductor, and an SMD switch for the light bar. Main power, DC/AC module and blue buttons are also mentioned, not counted.

Eight MOSFETs on two heat sinks, four on each. The page names PCsemic as maker of the first group (two on the left marked GEANGFD, two on the right printed RBANGFD) and only counts four more on the other heat sink.
Transformer in the inverter module; its magnetic core is insulated by tape.
Five CapXon 1000 uF 63 V electrolytic capacitors in parallel on the DC input (input filter).
Three SongChuan relays with 12 V coils: 507-2AH-F-C (12 A), 507H-1AH-F-S (17 A) and 210H-2AH-F-C (16 A).
RUNDA RS7015B12VH-RA, 12 V 0.26 A. The page shows one fan and says the two fans on the other side are the same, so three in the inverter module.
Two heat sinks in the inverter module, four MOSFETs fixed on each.
100 A fuse on the DC side of the inverter module.
GigaDevice GD32F303CET6 MCUs, one for primary and one for secondary inverter control (page lists 120 MHz, 512 KB flash).
GigaDevice GD32F303RCT6 MCU on the battery protection PCB (page lists 120 MHz, 256 KB flash, PWM signal output).
8.000 MHz crystal for the battery protection MCU.
32.768 kHz crystal for the battery protection MCU.
8.000 MHz crystal for each inverter MCU.
NOVOSENSE NSi6602BD isolation drivers, six, corresponding to the inverter MOSFETs.
0.5 mOhm sampling resistor for DC current detection.
100 Ohm cement resistor.
Silicon SCT2A25 buck chip, used to power the drive.
CapXon 330 uF 500 V filter capacitors (plural on the page, no count given), with heat sinks on both sides and a thermistor on a heat sink.
Two resonant capacitors, reinforced with glue.
Two blue STE Y capacitors.
Two SINCERITY 1 uF safety X2 capacitors.
STE 20D471K varistor.
Ygen W55-12A overload protector, used for overload protection.
Two common-mode chokes wound on magnetic rings.
Filter inductor fixed with zip ties.
comps.loc: Board not named (caption sits among the AC input protection PCB captions)

comps.spec: Resonant inductor whose magnetic core is insulated by tape.
Two SP1060L Schottky diodes connected in parallel, TO-277 package, 10 A 60 V. Used to block DC input current flow when reverse biased.
Betterfuse fuse marked 477, 20 A. The page gives two identical captions for it, one after the battery-pack XT30 connector and one after the battery communication connectors.
comps.loc: Fast-charging PCB, near the battery pack connectors

comps.spec: AC input socket inside the hidden cover. The page says the input socket is connected via a connector and the AC input via binding posts.
XT30 connector, named for the battery pack and for the car charger socket.
MPS MP9486A buck, 100 V in, 3.5 A out, with a 33 uH inductor.
Belling BL1084 linear regulator in TO-252 package.
Belling BL24C256 memory chip, 256 Kbit.
3PEAK LM393A dual voltage comparator.
3PEAK LM2904A dual op-amp.
Two heat sinks on the back of the fast-charging PCB, each with a thermistor.
Two ring-wound inductors with bakelite insulation.
Buck chip marked A6163K with a 15 uH SMD inductor.
Renesas ISL81401 synchronous buck controller, 40 V, driving two buck MOSFETs for the car port output.
Silicon SCT2A25 buck chip with integrated MOSFET, 5.5-100 V in, 2 A out, with a 47 uH inductor.

Renesas ISL81601 synchronous buck-boost chips, two on the board. The page gives a working voltage of 60 V for the first, which charges the built-in battery; the other is also an ISL81601 and is used for buck control.
iSmartWare SW3516P USB-C controllers with a 5 A synchronous buck, up to 100 W PD.
iSmartWare SW3526 USB-A buck controller, 3.5 A synchronous buck, with a 22 uH inductor.
Four PCsemic MOSFETs for the synchronous buck-boost chip (ISL81601).
Two MOSFETs for power-supply control.
Two synchronous buck MOSFETs for the USB-C ports.
Two buck MOSFETs for the car port output.
Two TVS diodes between the USB-C sockets for electrostatic protection.
TVS marked C70 for overvoltage protection.
Three CapXon 100 uF 100 V electrolytic input-filter capacitors.
Runic RS8552 op-amp for signal acquisition and amplification.
Espressif ESP32-C3-MINI-1 wireless module.
LCD display module. Driver chip i-Core CS1621 is on the back of the module.
LED light bar with 18 LED lamp beads, switched by an SMD button.
